title: Fixed Closed Corrugated Enclosure and Two-Level Cross Struts
description: One wholly newly authored complete dry internally-braced-cofferdam-inspired architectural display. One continuous thick corrugated rectangular perimeter closes around all four corners with a genuine open top and a full separate flat ground floor. Two complete rectangular inner waler frames run around the enclosure at separated heights, each with an actual large central opening. Three whole transverse struts at each level join the opposite long waler sides; four whole upper diagonal corner knees connect adjacent frame sides. Every wall fold, corner, waler and strut is newly authored together. The full interior remains open between the brace rows, with no soil, water or installed worksite. Unlike the prior one-sided retaining curtain with rear tie rods and separate anchors, this whole closed perimeter carries inward encircling frames and full cross-span bracing on both levels. Unlike the timber flying shore, there are no isolated wall-bearing plates, central raker/cheek joint or absent host walls. The entire finite-thickness corrugated curtain is one closed editable body, not repeated independent sheet assets or an asserted interlocking system. All numeric geometry new, no old wall, shore, tieback, basin or brace mesh imported or extracted. Four constant opaque untextured PBR appearances, metres native Z up, whole bounds-centred finite ground sole, one architectural model zero scenes. Empty static illustrative geometry only, not a construction detail or designed temporary work. No soil pressure, excavation sequence, water seal, dewatering, sheet interlock, weld, bolt, strut compression, buckling, anchoring, load, stability, access, installation, fabrication, structural or civil safety capability made or verified. No rigging, animation or interaction.
